court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Dispute between husband and wife over receivership/possession of a leased hotel business against the landlord; no issue of letting rooms or boarding/lodging regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Commercial lease of manufacturing floor space; landlord's repair entry held not an eviction. No lodging/boarding issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Purely procedural landlord-tenant dispute over pleading a breach-of-repair-covenant as defense vs. counterclaim in a summary possession action. No lodging/boarding content.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Civil-rights case on whether a bootblack stand is a 'place of public accommodation' under 1895 anti-discrimination statute; unrelated to letting dwellings or boarding-house regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Wife (a longtime boarding-house keeper) sues husband's estate for board furnished to him. Boarding-house keeping is background fact only; the holding concerns sufficiency of proof of an implied reimbursement obligation between spouses, not the legal character or regulation of letting/boarding.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Procedural sufficiency of a dispossess petition brought by an executor's agent, and tenant estoppel to deny landlord's title. No lodging/boarding content.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Replevin dispute over a saloon tenant's trade fixtures (urinals, partition, awning) after chattel-mortgage foreclosure. No lodging/boarding issue.

Demurrer in an easement-abandonment action; defendant built an apartment hotel where private stables once stood, but that fact is incidental to the easement pleading question, not the letting practice.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Deed-covenant construction case (does 'tenement house' restriction bar a modern apartment house). Discusses that hotels/boarding houses were common and unrestricted uses in 1873, but the holding turns on covenant interpretation of building type, not on the legal character or regulation of paying-occupant arrangements themselves.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Vendor-purchaser incumbrance dispute over a restrictive covenant against noxious trades; a cited precedent lists 'tenement house, brewery, lager beer saloon' among prohibited uses, but this case itself does not address letting or boarding-house regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Libel action over a newspaper's claim that plaintiffs' commercial hotel 'has a bad reputation'; holding concerns pleading of special damages in a property libel, not the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Upholds application of the 1901 Tenement House Act (police-power regulation) against a builder whose construction was not yet under way when the act took effect. Tenement houses here are permanent multi-family apartment buildings, not short-term lodging/boarding houses, and no occupancy or compensated-occupancy issue is presented (dispute is purely about timing of a construction permit); outside the corpus's boarding/lodging-house regulation focus.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Sets the duration of an innkeeper's liability for a departed guest's baggage; a tort/bailment-duty question collateral to the hotel relationship, not a holding on the legality or regulation of letting/lodging arrangements.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Conversion action by an evicted hotel-operator tenant against the landlord over hotel supplies left behind after dispossession. Landlord-tenant/personal-property dispute, not about letting or regulating lodging.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Party-wall agreement dispute between adjoining lot owners; no lodging/boarding content.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: Murder prosecution arising from a fight between rival sailors'-boarding-house 'runners.' Boarding houses appear only as the parties' employers/context; the holding concerns jury instructions on self-defense evidence and character evidence, not the legal character or regulation of boarding houses.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Statutory default lease-term rule (Real Prop. Law §202) applied to an oral hiring of commercial premises for a business. No lodging/boarding issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Whether a conventional landlord-tenant relationship arose by implication over a saloon lease assignment, based on rent-payment conduct. No lodging/boarding issue.
